LESSON: WRITING 8.5.1 ASSESSMENT OF WRITING

Grade: Grade 8
Subject: ENGLISH
Strand: Strand 8
Topic 8.5: Writing 8.5.1 Assessment of writing

SECTION 1: WELCOME

Hello! This is a study lesson on Writing 8.5.1 Assessment of writing. Read the explanation, follow every worked example, then do the practice. This is original CBC Learn content written from KICD outcomes — not a copy of a commercial textbook.

Big question: what the others have done. 1. How does a text with errors make you feel?

SECTION 2: WHAT YOU WILL LEARN

By the end of this lesson, you will be able to:

1. identify errors in an essay written by self or peers
2. appreciate the importance feedback to improve a composition

SECTION 3: STUDY NOTES (READ AND LEARN)

WHAT YOU ARE LEARNING: WRITING 8.5.1 ASSESSMENT OF WRITING
This lesson teaches Writing 8.5.1 Assessment of writing for Grade 8 ENGLISH.

STUDY STEPS
1. identify errors in an essay written by self or peers
   Practise this until you can do it without help.
2. appreciate the importance feedback to improve a composition
   Practise this until you can do it without help.

HOW TO SHOW UNDERSTANDING
Explain the idea in your own words, give one Kenyan example, then complete the practice tasks.

SECTION 4: QUICK EXAMPLES

Example 1: Describe Writing 8.5.1 Assessment of writing using something at your school.

Example 2: Give a home/community example from your county.

Example 3: Teach a younger child one idea from this lesson in simple words.

SECTION 5: PRACTICE NOW

1. Underline the key ideas about Writing 8.5.1 Assessment of writing above.
2. Explain Writing 8.5.1 Assessment of writing to a parent using one local example.
3. Write or draw three things that prove you understand Writing 8.5.1 Assessment of writing.

SECTION 6: WORK TO DO (HOME / REVISION)

1. Write five sentences about Writing 8.5.1 Assessment of writing with school or home examples.
2. Answer: Why is Writing 8.5.1 Assessment of writing important for a Grade 8 learner?
3. Prepare a one-minute oral presentation for a parent or teacher.

SECTION: THINK ABOUT IT

1. what the others have done. 1. How does a text with errors make you feel?
2. What are some of the common mistakes we make in our writing?

SECTION: REMEMBER

1. identify errors in an essay written by self or peers
2. appreciate the importance feedback to improve a composition

Now complete the Revision Quiz. Open Answers only after you finish.

— CBC Learn · Original study notes from KICD outcomes (Strategy 2)
